name: Access0x1ReceiptHook
description: Emits a receipt for every swap through any pool that names it. A swap may claim a merchant and order in hook data; the receipt's flag is true only when that merchant is active on the Access0x1 Router and the swap was made by its own payout or owner wallet. Takes no fee, holds no funds, has no admin, and cannot make a swap revert.

reasons: No dynamic fee and no returns-delta bit.
Swaps work with empty hookData; a claim is optional.
Deployed addresses start 0x8D/0x40/0xd8, 0x35/0x82/0x37 and 0x47/0x49/0x70: none starts 0x91.

pool.fee: Any. The hook does not read or set it.

state.name: trustedRouter
writtenBy: setRouterTrust, by the merchant's owner on the Router

deltas.settledBy: Nobody. Without the afterSwapReturnDelta bit the PoolManager does not read it.

externalCalls.trust: Trusted for merchant records. Gas-capped at 50,000 and wrapped in try/catch: a failure gives an unverified receipt, never a failed swap.

externalCalls.target: a router the merchant's owner trusts
externalCalls.trust: Trusted only for that merchant, by that merchant's choice. Gas-capped and wrapped in try/catch.

accessControl.caller: the merchant's current owner on the Router
accessControl.enforcedBy: live read of merchants(id).owner; reverts NotMerchantOwner

securityAssumptions: The Access0x1 Router reports merchant records truthfully.
A router a merchant trusts reports its user truthfully; a lying router can only affect that merchant's own receipts.
doesNotGuarantee: Does not stop anyone from CLAIMING a merchant: an unverified receipt still names the claimed id. Consumers must read the verified flag.
Does not check that the swap paid the merchant or matches an order; orderRef is the swapper's word.
Does not verify swaps by a merchant wallet through a router the merchant has not trusted, other than a direct PoolManager caller.

invariants.statement: The hook's address carries exactly afterSwap, mask 0x40.
The merchant's own wallet swapping through a router the merchant trusts gives a verified receipt.
An untrusted router's report is ignored.
A stranger's claim is recorded but not verified.
An inactive merchant is never verified.
A failing registry leaves the swap settled and the receipt unverified.
Only the merchant's owner can trust a router.
No hook data of any length can fail a swap; only 64 bytes is read as a claim.
